answer: A concrete mechanism can make fake identities expensive. Each new identity needs two sponsors from separate standing groups, both listed in the inlet registry. Sponsors lock collateral in the ember pool that is seized if a random audit finds the recruit's work copied or empty. First rewards stay escrowed in the summit ledger until three unrelated peers verify a real task receipt. A farm cannot bootstrap itself: N fake identities require N independent sponsors with clean histories and money at risk, so headcount carries a capital cost, not just a registration fee.
